sections.label: GDP, productivity and income growth
sections.summary: GDP grew 3.6%, productivity and real median income rose, and 21 of 23 Industry Transformation Maps were launched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 3.6%1, up from 2.4% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our productivity growth was 4.5% as measured by real value-added per actual hour worked, and 3.8% as measured by real value-added per worker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Real median income2	for Singapore Citizens rose by 5.3%3 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For 2018, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) expects growth to be more broad-based across sectors but moderated from the high of 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the support of businesses, Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) and unions, we have launched 21 out of the proposed 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme and CIT rebate
sections.summary: WCS is extended three years with declining co-funding, and the YA2018 CIT rebate is raised to 40%, capped at $15,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, I will extend the Wage Credit Scheme (WCS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For 2017, we expect to pay out more than $800 million to more than 90,000 firms, for wage increases given to more than 600,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will extend WCS for three more years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: WCS will provide 20% co-funding for 2018, 15% for 2019 and 10% for 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will cost about $1.8 billion over the next three years  .

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For Year of Assessment (YA) 2018, I will raise the CIT rebate to 40% of tax payable, capped at $15,000.

sections.label: Employment support for workers
sections.summary: Professional Conversion Programmes helped over 3,700 mid-career individuals, and the Work Trial scheme becomes the Career Trial scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, the Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) have helped more than 3,700 mid-career individuals take up new jobs last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we will strengthen employment support for lower- to middle-income workers in various ways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This includes upgrading the current Work Trial scheme into a Career Trial scheme, with higher funding support for workers to try out new careers	 .

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant and licensing deduction
sections.summary: Grants for adopting off-the-shelf technologies are streamlined into the PSG, and the licensing payments tax deduction is raised to 200%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, we will support businesses to buy and use new solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will streamline existing grants supporting the adoption of pre-scoped, off-the-shelf technologies into a single Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG)	 .

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the expiry of the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme, the tax deduction on licensing payments has reverted to 100% for YA2019 and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will raise this to 200%, capped at $100,000 of licensing payments per year.

sections.label: IP registration and R&D deductions
sections.summary: The IP registration fee cap is $100,000 yearly, and the tax deduction for Singapore R&D expenses rises from 150% to 250%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will be capped at $100,000 of IP registration fees per year  .

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also raise the tax deduction for qualifying expenses incurred on R&D done in Singapore, from 150% to 250%  .

sections.label: IP commercialisation and transformation programmes
sections.summary: NRF and Temasek launch an IP Commercialisation Vehicle, and up to $500 million supports the Aviation and Maritime Transformation Programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have various programmes to translate our public sector research efforts into commercially viable applications, and we will build on these.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, the National Research Foundation (NRF) and Temasek will launch an NRF Temasek IP Commercialisation Vehicle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At least $100 million will go into this joint venture – $50 million from the Government, and at least $50 million from Temasek  .

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To strengthen our status as an air and sea hub, we will launch an Aviation Transformation Programme (ATP) and a Maritime Transformation Programme (MTP) this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The solutions that emerge can be rapidly adopted in other parts of Singapore, or even exported overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will provide support of up to $500 million for the two programmes, with additional matching investments expected from industry partners  .

sections.label: TeSA emerging digital skills funding
sections.summary: TeSA will support learning of emerging digital skills and an additional $145 million is set aside over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: TeSA will also support more people to learn emerging digital skills, such as in data analytics, artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT) and cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will set aside an additional $145 million for TeSA over the next three years  .

sections.label: ASEAN Leadership Programme under LDI
sections.summary: Companies committed to train almost 200 Singaporeans, and a new ASEAN Leadership Programme will launch this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since it started last year, companies have committed to train almost 200 Singaporeans, with over 180 more in the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we will launch a new ASEAN Leadership Programme under the LDI to help our business leaders build networks and plan business expansions in Southeast Asian markets.

sections.label: Employment rate for older residents
sections.summary: Singapore's employment rate for residents aged 65 and above rose from 14.4% in 2007 to 25.8% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the close cooperation of the tripartite partners, Singapore's employment rate for residents aged 65 and above rose from 14.4% in 2007 to 25.8% in 2017.

sections.label: PACT scheme and $800 million
sections.summary: Partnership support measures will be integrated into a PACT scheme, with $800 million set aside over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Industry partners, like the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI), have made similar suggestions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will integrate various partnership support measures into a single Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT) scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For the three schemes that I mentioned earlier – PACT, the Productivity Solutions Grant and the Enterprise Development Grant – I will set aside $800 million over the next three years.

sections.label: Infrastructure Office for Asia agenda
sections.summary: An Infrastructure Office will bring together local and international firms to develop, finance and execute infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To contribute to Asia’s infrastructure agenda, we will set up an Infrastructure Office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This Office will bring together local and international firms from across the value chain, including infrastructure developers, institutional investors, multilaterals and legal, accounting and financial services providers, to develop, finance and execute infrastructure projects.

sections.label: Trade Association Hub at Jurong
sections.summary: SCCCI, with JTC and SPRING support, set up a Trade Association Hub where over 30 TACs share facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For instance, SCCCI, with support from JTC and SPRING, has set up a Trade Association Hub (TA Hub) at Jurong Town Hall, where more than 30 TACs share facilities and resources.

sections.label: Transport Integrated Platform and LEAD
sections.summary: TRIP integrates existing systems to track container trucks and reduce idling, and about $45 million was committed through LEAD for some 50 projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, it launched the Transport Integrated Platform (TRIP), which integrates several existing systems into a single digital platform, to enable easier tracking of container trucks and reduce idling time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the last two years, about $45 million has been committed through LEAD for some 50 projects.

sections.label: Funding for three programmes
sections.summary: $250 million will be set aside for these three programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For these three programmes, we will set aside $250 million  .

sections.label: Carbon tax from 2019
sections.summary: A carbon tax will apply from 2019 to all facilities producing 25,000 tonnes or more of greenhouse gas emissions a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage companies to further reduce emissions, I announced last year that we intend to implement a carbon tax from 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will proceed with a carbon tax on all facilities producing 25,000 tonnes or more of greenhouse gas emissions in a year.

sections.label: Carbon tax rates and review
sections.summary: The carbon tax will be $5 per tonne from 2019 to 2023, reviewed by 2023, and intended to rise to $10 to $15 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The carbon tax will be $5 per tonne of greenhouse gas emissions in the first instance, from 2019 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will review the carbon tax rate by 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We intend to increase it to a rate of between $10 and $15 per tonne of emissions by 2030.

sections.label: Grants and carbon tax revenue
sections.summary: More grants and support will help companies and households enhance energy efficiency, with nearly $1 billion in carbon tax revenue expected in the first five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To give companies and households a strong push in the first five years when we introduce the carbon tax, we will provide more grants and support to help them enhance energy efficiency and reduce emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect to collect carbon tax revenue of nearly $1 billion in the first five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To achieve our goal of reducing emissions intensity as soon as possible, I am prepared to spend more than this in the initial five years, to support worthwhile projects which deliver the necessary abatement in emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I urge companies to do their part for a higher quality living environment for all, by putting in meritorious proposals for emissions abatement and energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside funds starting from 2019 to enhance support for companies, including SMEs and power generation companies, to improve energy efficiency.

sections.label: Household impact and U-Save
sections.summary: The carbon tax impact on households is about 1% of electricity and gas expenses, and eligible HDB households receive $20 more U-Save yearly from 2019 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For our households, the impact of the carbon tax will be small, at about 1% of total electricity and gas expenses, on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Still, to help households adjust, I will provide additional U-Save for three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Eligible HDB households will each receive $20 more per year, from 2019 to 2021.

sections.label: Government support for citizens
sections.summary: The Government has increased support over the past decade through schemes like MediShield Life, Pioneer Generation Package, Workfare and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the past decade, the Government has increased support for our citizens, providing greater assurance through schemes like MediShield Life and the Pioneer Generation Package, while giving extra help to those with less through Workfare and Silver Support.

sections.label: Edusave and financial assistance increases
sections.summary: Edusave contributions will rise to $230 for primary and $290 for secondary students, and MOE bursaries for pre-university students will rise to $900.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, we will increase the annual Edusave contributions provided by the Government from $200 to $230 for each primary school student, and from $240 to $290 for each secondary school student.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Third, we will increase the support to students from lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will enhance the Ministry of Education (MOE) Financial Assistance Scheme by raising the annual bursary quantum for pre-university students from $750 to $900 and updating the income eligibility criteria.

sections.label: Cost of these schemes
sections.summary: These schemes will cost close to $200 million per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Overall, these schemes will cost close to $200 million per year.

sections.label: PHG for resale flat families
sections.summary: The PHG for families buying a resale flat to live with their parents or children will increase to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, we will increase the PHG for families buying a resale flat to live with their parents or children to $30,000.

sections.label: Extension of rebates
sections.summary: The rebates will be extended for another year, costing $126 million and benefiting about 900,000 households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will extend these rebates for another year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This will cost $126 million and benefit about 900,000 households	 .

sections.label: Aged person scheme qualifying age
sections.summary: The qualifying age for the levy concession under the aged person scheme will be raised from 65 to 67 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In light of the improving life expectancy and health of Singaporeans, we will raise the qualifying age for the levy concession under the aged person scheme from 65 to 67 years.

sections.label: FDW levy increase
sections.summary: The monthly levy for the first and second FDW employed without levy concession will be raised to $300 and $450.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For the first and second FDW employed without levy concession, the monthly levy will be raised from $265 today to $300 and $450 respectively.

sections.label: CNS nationwide expansion
sections.summary: CNS will be expanded nationwide by 2020 to reach out to and serve more seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To reach out to and serve more seniors, we will expand CNS nationwide by 2020.

sections.label: Community Silver Trust top-up
sections.summary: A $300 million top-up will be provided to the Community Silver Trust, which matches donations to eligible VWOs providing long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, I will provide a $300 million top-up to the Community Silver Trust (CST), which provides dollar-for-dollar matching for donations to eligible VWOs providing long-term care services.

sections.label: Strengthening Social Service Offices
sections.summary: Over five years, the role and capabilities of Social Service Offices will be strengthened to coordinate support for those in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we will strengthen the role and capabilities of our Social Service Offices (SSOs) to better coordinate the efforts of Government agencies, VWOs and community partners in providing more holistic and citizen-centred support to those in need.

sections.label: Extending IPC tax deduction
sections.summary: The 250% tax deduction for donations to Institutions of a Public Character will be extended for three years until 31 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Many of us share Mdm Patma’s spirit and are actively giving back to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I am heartened that over the last decade, our volunteerism rate has doubled, from around 17% to 35%6.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: At the same time, total donations have increased from around $2 billion in 2011 to $2.7 billion in 20157.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To foster this spirit of giving in our people, we will enhance support for measures that encourage everyone to contribute to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I will extend the 250% tax deduction for donations made to Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs) for another three years, until 31 December 2021  .

sections.label: CDC matching grant cap
sections.summary: From FY2018 onwards, the annual matching grant cap for CDCs will be increased from $24 million to $40 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: From financial year (FY) 2018 onwards, I will increase the current annual matching grant cap for CDCs from $24 million to $40 million  .

sections.label: Healthcare spending more than doubled
sections.summary: Healthcare spending rose from $3.9 billion in FY2011 to an estimated $10.2 billion in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Since the start of this decade, we have more than doubled our healthcare spending, from $3.9 billion in FY2011 to an estimated $10.2 billion in FY2018.

sections.label: Elderly rise and healthcare spending
sections.summary: By 2030 the elderly will rise by about 450,000 to 900,000, with more hospitals, polyclinics and eldercare, and healthcare spending rising to almost 3% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: By 2030, the total number of elderly will increase by about 450,000, to 900,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Within the next five years, we will build six more general and community hospitals, four new polyclinics, and more nursing homes and eldercare centres around the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: All in all, we expect our average annual healthcare spending to rise from 2.2% of GDP today to almost 3% of GDP over the next decade.

sections.label: Preschool sector spending by 2022
sections.summary: The Government will spend $1.7 billion per year on the preschool sector by 2022, double current annual spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister announced last year, we will spend $1.7 billion per year on the preschool sector by 2022, double our annual spending now.

sections.label: Reducing Ministries' block budget growth
sections.summary: From FY2019, the allowed growth rate of Ministries' block budgets will be cut from 0.4 to 0.3 times GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Currently, Ministries' block budgets are allowed to grow at 0.4 times of GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I will reduce this rate to 0.3 times from FY2019.

sections.label: New Rail Infrastructure Fund
sections.summary: A new Rail Infrastructure Fund will be set up, starting with a $5 billion injection in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We now have $4 billion in the fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This year, we will set up a new Rail Infrastructure Fund to save up for major rail lines ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will start with an injection of $5 billion in FY2018.

sections.label: GST rise for recurrent spending
sections.summary: To avoid borrowing for recurrent spending, the Government plans to raise GST from 7% to 9% sometime between 2021 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We should not borrow for recurrent spending, because that will put the burden of recurrent spending on future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Therefore, to support these recurrent needs, the Government plans to raise GST by two percentage points, from 7% to 9%, sometime in the period from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: GST increase revenue
sections.summary: Raising GST by two percentage points will provide revenue of almost 0.7% of GDP per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Increasing GST by two percentage points will provide us with revenue of almost 0.7% of GDP per year.

sections.label: NIR contribution growth
sections.summary: NIRC more than doubled from $7 billion in FY2009 to an estimated $15.9 billion in FY2018, now the largest revenue contributor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years since the implementation of the NIR framework, the NIR contribution (NIRC) has more than doubled from $7 billion in FY2009 to an estimated $15.9 billion in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: NIRC is now the largest contributor to our revenues, larger than any single tax, including GST and corporate and personal income taxes.

sections.label: Spending expected NIR
sections.summary: Currently, up to 50% of expected NIR is spent and the remainder kept in Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Currently, we spend up to 50% of expected NIR and keep the remainder in our Reserves.

sections.label: Property tax and BSD
sections.summary: A progressive property tax system was introduced in 2010 and made more progressive in 2013, and the top BSD rate rises from 3% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We also introduced a progressive property tax system for residential properties in 2010 and made it more progressive in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This year, I will raise the top marginal Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD) rate for residential properties from 3% to 4%.

sections.label: GST on imported services
sections.summary: GST on imported services will be introduced with effect from 1 January 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Next, to make sure that our tax system remains fair and resilient in a digital economy, I will introduce GST on imported services with effect from 1 January 2020.

sections.label: Higher than forecast revenue
sections.summary: This is higher than the $1.9 billion or 0.4% of GDP forecasted a year ago, an increase of $7.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This is higher than the $1.9 billion or 0.4% of GDP forecasted a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This increase of $7.7 billion is mainly due to exceptional Statutory Board contributions of $4.6 billion, primarily from MAS, and increased stamp duty collections of $2 billion due to the recent property market pickup.

sections.label: Rail fund, ElderShield subsidies, hongbao
sections.summary: Sets aside $5 billion for the Rail Infrastructure Fund, $2 billion for ElderShield support, and gives Singaporeans aged 21 and above a $300, $200 or $100 hongbao.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, I will set aside $5 billion in the Rail Infrastructure Fund that I spoke about earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Next, I will set aside $2 billion for premium subsidies and other forms of support for Singaporeans when the ElderShield review is complete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: All Singaporeans aged 21 and above in 2018 will enjoy a "hongbao" of $300, $200 or $100, depending on their income.

sections.label: Expected Budget deficit
sections.summary: Expects a slight overall Budget deficit of $0.6 billion, or 0.1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: On the whole, we expect a slight overall Budget deficit of $0.6 billion, or 0.1% of GDP	 .

sections.label: Approval of financial policy, adjournment
sections.summary: States the Question on approving the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2018 to 31 March 2019, and that the debate stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2018 to 31 March 2019." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
